A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM3-I and its instruction-guided extension of SAM3. All nine pages of v1 and eighteen pages of v3 are readable, including figures, tables, equations, and v3's Appendices A–E. v1 has no appendix. The substantial revisions remain reliably comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original PACO-LVIS-Instruct segmentation results, baseline comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative predictions in Tables 1–2 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v3 reports original HMPL-Instruct, RefCOCO, and Ref-ZOM evaluations, expanded ablations, sensitivity studies, and qualitative predictions in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the frozen SAM3 backbone and cascaded adapters but adds instruction contrastive and parent-rank concept anchoring losses. It changes one-way mask KL alignment to symmetric KL and replaces cross-entropy between branch predictions with ground-truth supervision for both branches. The reported adapter activation also changes from ReLU to GELU.

E1.justification: PACO-LVIS-Instruct evolves into HMPL-Instruct with explicit part-level annotations and one-to-many subset grounding, including 2,941 subset samples, substantially expanding v1's reported object-level dataset. v3 also evaluates RefCOCO and Ref-ZOM in Table 4; these were not evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The main SAM3 comparison drops the Qwen3-VL-2B agent variant while retaining the 8B variant under the shortened SAM3 Agent name. v3 adds LISA and UniPixel to HMPL-Instruct comparisons in Tables 3 and 8, and evaluates LISA, ReLA, UniPixel, and SAM3 Agent on the external benchmarks in Table 4.

E3.justification: The ablation protocol expands from component removal in v1 Table 2 to stagewise training, individual-loss additions, and a single-adapter control in v3 Table 5, with explicit rho and margin sweeps in Appendix C. Dataset sample totals also change. The gIoU/P@50 metrics, inherited PACO-LVIS split policy, batch size 32, and three-round agent limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands the retained curriculum and alignment analyses with C-Adapter-only and cascaded-versus-single-adapter controls, tests of the new losses, and hyperparameter sensitivity studies. Tables 3 and 8 analyze target cardinality and object/part performance, while Figure 8 adds qualitative comparisons with UniPixel on challenging instruction-grounding cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The uncertainty-aware hard-region loss concerns training supervision and does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports SAM3-I simple/complex gIoU/P@50 of 54.0/59.6 and 51.0/56.4; v3 Table 2 reports 59.7/65.3 and 49.0/51.0 on the revised dataset and method. These are replaced results under changed conditions. Numerous results are added, including Table 4's RefCOCO gIoU of 76.3 versus UniPixel's 78.1 and Ref-ZOM gIoU of 73.6 versus 67.0.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4 introduces formal definitions for weighted bidirectional instruction contrastive learning and margin-based concept anchoring in Equations 1–4. Equations 5–6 substantively revise the mask-alignment and hard-region objectives. These expand and alter the mathematical formulation rather than merely restating v1's equations; neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of extending SAM3 to instructions while preserving concept grounding remains. However, v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate HMPL-Instruct into a unified benchmark contribution covering object/part targets and one-to-one, one-to-many, and one-to-all grounding. This substantially expands v1's stated data contribution and incorporates capabilities previously described as future directions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets subset-grounding results as evidence against category-level overfitting and adds explanations of contrastive weighting, concept anchoring, and adapter specialization. Its limitations retain cardinality bias but add the absence of dense grounded understanding and conversational capabilities. v1's specific adaptive-routing/MoE and broader ReasonSeg evaluation outlooks are removed.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D add detailed annotation workflows, point-to-mask assignment, JSON export information, adapter insertion sites, bottleneck dimension 64, 1024-dimensional four-head attention, and approximately 311.9M trainable parameters. v3 also specifies rho, margin, and temperature settings and explicitly states dataset availability alongside code. The existing hardware and batch-size disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial related-work review in Appendix A covering open-vocabulary, referring, and reasoning segmentation, plus benchmark positioning in Table 1. New cited work includes UniPixel, MMR, InstructPart, Sa2VA, and contrastive-learning research. The earlier MoE-related citations disappear with the corresponding outlook, materially changing positioning beyond the SAM-family overview.

P1.justification: Existing abstract, introduction, SAM overview, and training explanations are extensively rewritten. Section 5 becomes dataset-centered, experiments gain separate metrics, quantitative, qualitative, and ablation subsections, and Discussion and Outlook is replaced by separate limitations. Appendices A–E reorganize related work, construction details, experiments, implementation, and artifact statements.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn to show the new embedding losses, and v3 adds dataset, granularity, benchmark, and sensitivity tables plus annotation-tool and example figures. Existing visuals are matched: v1 Figure 5 becomes v3 Figure 4, and v1 Figure 4 moves to the appendix as Figure 5. Typography, captions, and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v1's narrow feasibility study through external benchmark comparisons, subset and part-level evaluations, and direct controls testing the cascaded-adapter design. Appendix D resolves important implementation omissions, while the expanded mathematical definitions and annotation documentation improve reproducibility. Training and split details for the new external comparisons remain sparse, and statistical uncertainty remains absent, but the gains in evidential support and technical completeness are substantial. Changed headline scores alone do not establish a same-setting accuracy improvement.
